subject: Day 35: order Suzuki recordings
bodyText:
Today's focus
Week 6 is the first sustainable inflection point: the crying curve is at or just past peak, and Avi is now smiling spontaneously at faces. Today's lever is a one-time setup task with a multi-year payoff: decide on a first instrument and start passive listening exposure.

Action items
- Decide on a first instrument with Noah and Anoushka today: violin (Suzuki's original), piano, or cello. The choice mostly sets which recordings you order; formal lessons are still about three years out, around age 3-4. Suzuki Association of the Americas: https://suzukiassociation.org/
- Order the Book 1 and Book 2 listening recordings for that instrument. Daily passive listening from this age carries no downside and is the single highest-leverage Suzuki prep step. Suzuki Association of the Americas: https://suzukiassociation.org/
- Schedule Avi's 2-month well visit if it is not yet booked; the window is day 56-70 and the rotavirus first dose must land by about day 104, so do not let it drift. AAP periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/care-delivery-approaches/periodicity-schedule/

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Hiccups during or after feeds and wet sneezing are normal autonomic noise at this age and need no action.
- [monitor] No social smile yet. About 80% of infants smile spontaneously by 8 weeks; if absent by then, flag it at the 2-month visit rather than now.
- [monitor] Forceful arching or painful spit-up after feeds. Document frequency and discuss reflux or cow's-milk-protein intolerance at the next visit.
- [call within 24h] A cluster of new symptoms together: poor feeding plus unusual lethargy plus decreased wet-diaper output.
- [call now] Rectal temperature 100.4F (38.0C) or higher, a pause in breathing, blue color around the lips, or seizure-like activity: call the pediatrician same-day, and dial 911 for blue lips or labored breathing!

Enrichment opportunities
- Play the new Suzuki recording softly during quiet play and feeds; aim to build toward roughly 30 minutes a day of background listening over the coming months. Live, participatory music matters more later, but early ear exposure is the Suzuki mother-tongue premise. Suzuki Association of the Americas: https://suzukiassociation.org/
- Build toward 30 minutes a day of tummy time across several short bouts as Avi now sustains 30-60 second head lifts. Distribute it after alert wake windows rather than after feeds. AAP Back to Sleep, Tummy to Play: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Read aloud with intentional pauses: read a line, look at him, pause, then read the next line. The serve-and-return cadence is the active ingredient even before he can talk and predicts later expressive language. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/

Upcoming
- Day 41 (this week): Anoushka's 6-week postpartum OB visit, typically with exercise clearance, contraception discussion, and a final mood screen.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit with the first major vaccine round (HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, IPV #1).
- Day 57-72: expect 24-48h of fussiness, low-grade fever, and extra drowsiness following the 2-month shots.
- Day 112-126: 4-month well visit with the second vaccine round (RV #2, DTaP #2, Hib #2, PCV #2, IPV #2).

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete

- Holds head up while on tummy
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-head-up-tummy/complete

- Hands relax open most of the time
  AAP window: day 35-90
  What to look for: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hands-open-mostly/complete

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete
